SOFTWARE ENGINEERING LAB PROJECT
SIGNATURE VERIFICATION SYSTEM USING CNN
(Prepared as part of PCA-I Submission)

ABSTRACT
A Signature Verification System is a software-based biometric authentication system designed to verify the genuineness
of a handwritten signature by comparing a submitted (query) signature against previously enrolled reference signatures of
the same individual. The system uses Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based image processing, feature
extraction, and classification to distinguish genuine signatures from forged ones while following general software
engineering principles that emphasize usability, reliability, maintainability, security, and clear requirements. The primary
objective is to support, rather than replace, forensic document examiners by providing an automated preliminary
verification decision and escalating uncertain or high-risk cases for manual review.
The expected output of the system is a structured verification result for each submitted signature, including a
genuine/forged classification, confidence score, and, where necessary, a recommendation for

ification result for each submitted signature, including a
genuine/forged classification, confidence score, and, where necessary, a recommendation for expert forensic review.
The system is intended to improve the speed and consistency of signature-based authentication in banking, legal, and
administrative processes while maintaining responsible use of automated decision-making. Overall, the Signature
Verification System Using CNN represents a software engineering approach to developing a reliable biometric
authentication solution that incorporates CNN-based signature feature extraction and classification, while
prioritizing accuracy, data security, and responsible escalation of uncertain cases.

SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS & SPECIFICATION
(1) INTRODUCTION
1.1. PURPOSE
The purpose of the Signature Verification System is to provide an accurate and reliable automated mechanism for
verifying the authenticity of handwritten signatures submitted by users. Signature samples are intended to be captured,
processed, and compared against enrolled reference signatures. A verification decision indicating whether a signature
is genuine or forged is to be generated. Users and administrators are also to be encouraged to refer uncertain or high-
risk cases to a qualified forensic document examiner. The system is designed to support signature-based
authentication and is not intended to replace qualified forensic experts in legally significant cases.
1.2. SCOPE
Limitations:-
• Cannot Provide Legal Certification — The system cannot independently issue legally binding forensic
certification of a signature's authenticity without expert human verification.

1.3. OVERVIEW
The Signature Verification System is designed as an automated biometric authentication system through which
handwritten signatures submitted by users can be verified against enrolled reference signatures.

(2) OVERALL DESCRIPTION
2.1. PRODUCT PERSPECTIVE
The Signature Verification System is designed as a biometric authentication application that verifies handwritten
signatures through an automated image-processing and matching pipeline. Users can enroll reference signatures and
submit query signatures, which are processed by the system to generate a verification decision.
From the user's perspective, a simple and accessible platform is provided for enrolling signature samples and
requesting verification of a submitted signature.
From the forensic expert's perspective, uncertain or high-risk verification cases may be escalated for manual review,
while routine verifications are handled automatically by the system.
From the administrator's perspective, the system can be managed and monitored, including maintenance of enrolled
signature data, user information, and overall system operations.

From the developer's perspective, the system consists of modules for user interaction, signature image processing,
feature extraction, matching and decision generation, database management, and administration. The system is
designed to be reliable, secure, maintainable, and scalable for future enhancements.

verification profile.

2.3. USER CHARACTERISTICS
• General Users/Account Holders: Users seeking to enroll their signature or verify a submitted signature against
enrolled records.

• Domain Awareness: Users are not expected to possess forensic document-examination knowledge and should
be able to understand the verification result provided by the system.
• Forensic Experts/Examiners: Experts may be involved when a case requires professional review, assessment,
or legal escalation.
• Administrators: Administrators should have basic technical knowledge to manage user information, monitor
system activities, and maintain enrolled signature data.
• Basic User Skills: Users should be able to perform basic operations such as registration, login, uploading
signature images, submitting verification requests, and providing feedback.

(3) SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS
3.1. EXTERNAL INTERFACE REQUIREMENTS
The External Interface Requirements section describes how the Signature Verification System interacts with users
and external systems or services.
3.1.1. User Interface
• A simple and user-friendly interface shall be provided for users to register and log in.
• Users shall be able to upload or capture reference and query signature images.
• An upload/scan-based interface shall be provided for submitting signatures for verification.
• Verification results, confidence scores, and recommendations shall be displayed clearly.
• Feedback options shall be provided for evaluating the accuracy of verification results.
• Administrators shall be provided with an interface for monitoring and managing system data.
3.1.2. Hardware Interface
• The system shall be accessible through devices such as computers, laptops, tablets, and smartphones.

• An internet-enabled device shall be required to access the system.
3.1.3. Software Interface
• The system shall interact with a database for storing user information, enrolled signature samples, verification
records, and feedback.
• CNN-based image-processing and pattern-matching techniques may be used for signature feature extraction,
classification, and comparison.
• External APIs may be integrated when required for additional authentication-related services.
• A secure authentication system shall be used for user registration and login.
• A payment gateway may be integrated for premium or bulk verification services.

3.3. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
3.3.1. Security
The system shall provide secure authentication, authorization, password protection, data protection, secure
communication, input validation, and secure session management to prevent unauthorized access to user and signature
data.
• Authentication: The system shall require users to authenticate themselves before accessing their personal and
signature information.
• Password Protection: User passwords shall be stored securely and shall not be stored in plain text.
• Authorization: Only authorized users shall be allowed to access their

User passwords shall be stored securely and shall not be stored in plain text.
• Authorization: Only authorized users shall be allowed to access their respective signature data and system
functions.
• Data Protection: Personal information, enrolled signature samples, verification records, and feedback shall be
protected against unauthorized access.
• Secure Communication: Data exchanged between the user, application, database, and external services shall be
transmitted through secure communication protocols such as HTTPS.
• Input Validation: User-provided data and uploaded signature images shall be validated before processing to
prevent invalid or harmful input.
• Session Security: The system shall securely terminate user sessions after logout to prevent unauthorized access.
• Administrative Access: Administrative functions shall be accessible only to authorized administrators.
• Data Privacy: The system shall avoid exposing signature or verification data to unauthorized users.

The system shall use a modular and well-documented structure so that individual modules can be easily tested,
modified, corrected, and enhanced without significantly affecting other system components.

data management, feature extraction, matching/decision generation, and administration.
• Easy Modification: Individual modules shall be modifiable without requiring major changes to unrelated
modules.
• Code Documentation: Important system functions and modules shall be properly documented.
• Error Handling: The system shall provide meaningful error messages to help identify and correct

updated and maintained easily.
• CNN Model Updates: The CNN-based feature extraction and classification components shall allow future
improvements, retraining, or replacement of the underlying CNN model.

• Scalability for Future Features: The system structure shall allow future features such as online notarization
integration and bank/institution API integration to be added.
• Testing: Individual modules should be testable independently to simplify debugging and maintenance.

reasonable response time while supporting multiple users and using system resources efficiently.
• Response Time: The system should provide a verification result within a reasonable time after receiving the
query signature.
• Query Processing: Signature verification requests should be processed efficiently without unnecessary delays.
• Login Performance: User registration and login operations should be completed within a reasonable response
time.
• Data Retrieval: Enrolled signature samples and verification history should be retrieved efficiently from the
database.

3.4. DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
The Design Constraints define the limitations and conditions that must be considered while designing the
Signature Verification System. These constraints are based on the proposed system's scope, dependencies, users, and
functions rather than formal forensic industry standards.
• Internet Dependency: The system shall require an active internet connection for communication
between the user, application, database, and CNN-based verification services.
• CNN Model Dependency: The quality of the verification result shall depend on the CNN model used for
signature feature extraction, classification, and matching.
• Limited Legal Functionality: The system shall provide an automated preliminary verification decision only. It
shall not independently issue legally certified forensic conclusions.
• Sample Quality Dependency: Verification accuracy shall depend on the quality and consistency of enrolled
reference signature samples provided by the user.

• Security Constraint: Personal and biometric signature data shall require secure authentication, controlled access,

• Device Compatibility: The system shall be designed to operate on commonly used devices such as smartphones,

• Simple User Interface: The interface shall be kept simple and understandable because users may have different

(4) CONCLUSION
The Signature Verification System demonstrates the application of Software Engineering principles in designing a
biometric-authentication-oriented system. The proposed system provides users with accessible signature verification
through functions such as user registration, login, signature sample enrollment, query submission, feature extraction,
verification result generation, forgery detection, sample management, feedback collection, and expert escalation. The
system is designed to support users with preliminary verification decisions while clearly maintaining the role of
qualified forensic document examiners for legally significant assessment.
Technically, the system follows a modular and database-oriented design, making the major functions easier to
maintain, test, modify, and extend. The use of a CNN model and reference-signature database enables submitted
signatures to be processed and verification results to be generated, while the forgery-detection stage provides

signatures to be processed and verification results to be generated, while the forgery-detection stage provides a
decision point for escalating uncertain or high-risk cases.
The design also addresses practical software qualities such as security, reliability, maintainability, performance,
and usability. Secure authentication and communication protect user and biometric data, while validation and error
handling improve reliability. The system remains dependent on internet connectivity, database availability, and the
CNN model, which are important practical design considerations.
Overall, the project demonstrates how requirements analysis, system design, functional and non-functional
requirements, data management, CNN-based feature processing, decision-making, and security considerations
can be combined to develop a structured signature verification system.
